evidence.claim: The constitutional text makes the president commander-in-chief, chair of the defense council, and the official who may proclaim a state of siege after consultation; it also requires cabinet, defense-council, and parliamentary authorization for declaring war.
evidence.title: Constitution
evidence.excerpt: The constitutional text makes the president commander-in-chief, chair of the defense council, and the official who may proclaim a state of siege after consultation; it also requires cabinet, defense-council, and parliamentary authorization for declaring war.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text; directly states the ruler's formal security powers and limits.
evidence.period_fit: This was the governing constitutional frame in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Formal office authority, not proof of how Tshisekedi personally exercised it.
contrary_evidence: Legal authority does not prove effective or prudent use in practice.

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch said the M23 summarily killed at least 29 civilians since mid-June 2022 and warned of possible Rwandan support for the group.
evidence.title: DR Congo: Resurgent M23 Rebels Target Civilians
evidence.excerpt: Human Rights Watch said the M23 summarily killed at least 29 civilians since mid-June 2022 and warned of possible Rwandan support for the group.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable rights-monitoring report with a precise casualty claim and date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows the violent environment Tshisekedi was responding to; the killings are attributable to the rebel group, not directly to him.
contrary_evidence: The report is adversarial to the rebel group; the Rwandan-support allegation is framed as concern rather than conclusively proven fact.

evidence.claim: In May 2022, BCNUDH documented 551 human-rights violations, 188 attributed to state agents, including at least 21 extrajudicial executions, while armed groups were responsible for 363 violations and at least 290 summary executions.
evidence.title: La situation des droits de l’homme dans le pays en mai 2022
evidence.publisher: Les Nations Unies en RD Congo
evidence.excerpt: In May 2022, BCNUDH documented 551 human-rights violations, 188 attributed to state agents, including at least 21 extrajudicial executions, while armed groups were responsible for 363 violations and at least 290 summary executions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN country-office monthly bulletin with quantified findings and attribution split.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-agent abuses are attributable to institutions under Tshisekedi's chain of command, though many incidents were carried out by provincial/security actors.
contrary_evidence: Armed groups still caused more violations overall, so the state was not the only or even main source of violence.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the state of siege had failed to improve security and instead enabled military authorities to undermine expression, assembly, and justice through blanket protest bans, military-court trials of civilians, and arbitrary detentions.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Justice and freedoms under siege in North-Kivu and Ituri
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the state of siege had failed to improve security and instead enabled military authorities to undermine expression, assembly, and justice through blanket protest bans, military-court trials of civilians, and arbitrary detentions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed rights-monitoring report grounded in contemporary field evidence and legal analysis.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 continuation of the state of siege.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The state of siege was Tshisekedi's declared policy; day-to-day abuses were often by military administrators, but the policy and its extensions were presidential-government choices.
contrary_evidence: The report focuses on the eastern provinces under state of siege, not the whole country, and some abuses were carried out by military authorities rather than direct presidential orders.

evidence.claim: HRW said authorities banned demonstrations and used excessive force; in April police killed five people during peaceful protests in Goma, Butembo, and Beni, and Tshisekedi later apologized to children involved only after appointing the police commander in charge of the roundup as mayor of Goma.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: HRW said authorities banned demonstrations and used excessive force; in April police killed five people during peaceful protests in Goma, Butembo, and Beni, and Tshisekedi later apologized to children involved only after appointing the police commander in charge of the roundup as mayor of Goma.
evidence.source_locator: Freedom of Expression, Peaceful Assembly, and Media section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent annual rights review with specific incidents and presidential response details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The killings were by police/provincial security forces; the apology and appointment are ruler-level decisions that show a mixed, weak accountability response.
contrary_evidence: The source mixes national and provincial actors, so direct presidential responsibility is partial rather than exclusive.

evidence.claim: The report says the government took some steps to identify, investigate, prosecute, and punish officials who committed abuses, but impunity remained common, particularly at higher levels.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: The report says the government took some steps to identify, investigate, prosecute, and punish officials who committed abuses, but impunity remained common, particularly at higher levels.
evidence.source_locator: executive summary and security-force accountability sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Mirror of a U.S. government country report with explicit accountability assessment.
evidence.period_fit: Covers the 2022 period and its immediate aftermath.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is ruler-relevant because it describes the administration's remedial record and the limits of enforcement under Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: The report also documents continued arbitrary arrests, protest repression, and abuse by security forces.

evidence.claim: Four military intelligence agents arrested and beat journalist Christophe Katembo Muthahinga in North Kivu over his traffic coverage.
evidence.title: DRC military detains, beats journalist Christophe Katembo Muthahinga
evidence.excerpt: Four military intelligence agents arrested and beat journalist Christophe Katembo Muthahinga in North Kivu over his traffic coverage.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent press-freedom monitor with direct victim testimony and agent identification.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is the closest 2022 press-abuse item to national-security command, because the perpetrators were military-intelligence agents, though the article still does not show a direct presidential order.
contrary_evidence: The incident is still a local operational abuse, not a documented order from the presidency.

evidence.claim: UNFPA said more than 97,000 GBV cases had been reported and taken care of in the DRC in 2022, while also stressing that the situation remained worrying and that government engagement was not enough on its own.
evidence.title: 16 Jours d’activisme contre les violences basées sur le genre : UNFPA RDC au coeur de la lutte contre les VBG
evidence.excerpt: UNFPA said more than 97,000 GBV cases had been reported and taken care of in the DRC in 2022, while also stressing that the situation remained worrying and that government engagement was not enough on its own.
evidence.source_locator: middle section of the article on the 16-days campaign
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN agency campaign report with a concrete 2022 caseload figure, but it is programmatic rather than an audit of state performance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects the response environment under Tshisekedi's government, but not a ruler-specific effectiveness finding.
contrary_evidence: The source simultaneously says the situation remained alarming, so the caseload is not a success metric.

evidence.claim: The government adopted a draft law amending the 1996 press law to extend it to freedom of information and online media in line with the constitution.
evidence.title: RDC: le gouvernement adopte le texte modifiant la loi sur l’exercice de la liberté de la presse
evidence.excerpt: The government adopted a draft law amending the 1996 press law to extend it to freedom of information and online media in line with the constitution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local reporting on a concrete cabinet decision with direct policy content.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a government-level reform under Tshisekedi's administration, though the article does not prove final enactment.
contrary_evidence: It is a draft-law adoption, not proof that the reform was passed, implemented, or improved safety on the ground.

evidence.claim: Tshisekedi told the Council that the Teke-Yaka conflict in Kwamouth had reached alarming proportions with deaths and material losses and that humanitarian care for displaced people was required.
evidence.title: Compte rendu de la soixante-douzième réunion du Conseil des Ministres
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi told the Council that the Teke-Yaka conflict in Kwamouth had reached alarming proportions with deaths and material losses and that humanitarian care for displaced people was required.
evidence.source_locator: communication item on the Kwamouth situation
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential council record with direct ruler communication and instructions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential attention and instructions, but the violence itself was local communal conflict rather than state violence.
contrary_evidence: The source is a response record, not evidence that the underlying communal violence was brought under control.

evidence.claim: After the Kishishe massacre, Tshisekedi ordered three days of national mourning and instructed the justice minister to open an internal investigation and pursue an international investigation without delay.
evidence.title: Compte rendu de la soixante-dix-neuvième réunion du Conseil des Ministres
evidence.excerpt: After the Kishishe massacre, Tshisekedi ordered three days of national mourning and instructed the justice minister to open an internal investigation and pursue an international investigation without delay.
evidence.source_locator: communication item on Kishishe and the follow-on instructions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential council record with explicit orders and accountability steps.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential response and command to investigate, though the massacre itself was committed by M23/Rwandan-backed forces rather than the state.
contrary_evidence: This is a response after mass violence, not proof that preventive domestic protection was effective beforehand.

evidence.claim: HRW said police were implicated in the Buhene killings and looting, but a year later there had been no meaningful inquiry or discipline; it also noted that Tshisekedi declared martial law and later appointed the police commander in charge of the attacks as deputy territory administrator.
evidence.title: DR Congo: No Inquiry into Police Role in Ethnic Killings
evidence.excerpt: HRW said police were implicated in the Buhene killings and looting, but a year later there had been no meaningful inquiry or discipline; it also noted that Tshisekedi declared martial law and later appointed the police commander in charge of the attacks as deputy territory administrator.
evidence.source_locator: main body paragraphs on inquiry failure and appointment
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Well-documented rights report with concrete attribution and accountability failure details.
evidence.period_fit: Still directly relevant in 2022 because the lack of inquiry and appointment both fall in the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The killings were local police/state-agent conduct; the appointment is a presidential decision that weakens the accountability signal.
contrary_evidence: Some violence predated the presidential appointment and originated in local ethnic conflict dynamics.

unresolved_gaps: No direct evidence of nuclear command-and-control, custody, accident-prevention, or safety-safeguard performance under Tshisekedi.
Independent compliance evidence for the Nairobi and Luanda processes remains thin.
Direct command-responsibility evidence and remedy follow-up for police and military abuses are still weak.
Direct evidence on institutional strengthening, political equality, and election-body independence is thin.
Independent 2022 implementation and household-level outcome evidence is still thin.
Direct ruler-attributable outcome data on health, education, nutrition, and protection remains sparse.
Direct evidence of Tshisekedi's own assets, family/business interests, campaign finance, and false statements is missing.
Completed outputs and adaptation under failure are not well documented for the major 2022 programs.
